statement: No agreement between the two leading compute jurisdictions sets verifiable limits on training compute or capabilities (official readouts, treaty texts; by 2028-06-30)
status_at_phase_end: Condition held throughout 2025: no bilateral agreement on compute or capability limits, verifiable or otherwise. Multilateral activity was non-binding (summit declaration not signed by Bloc A; UN scientific panel and dialogue limited to non-military, non-prescriptive work). The October leaders' meeting covered trade and chip controls but not AI risk limits. Bloc A's national AI plan framed AI as a race to win; Bloc B proposed a global AI cooperation body without verification provisions.

items.summary: At a multilateral AI summit, Bloc B and ~60 other states signed a non-binding declaration on 'inclusive and sustainable' AI; Bloc A (and one other leading AI state) declined, with Bloc A's vice-head of government warning against 'excessive regulation' and against cooperating with Bloc B.
items.detail: Bloc E AI Action Summit, 2025-02-10/11; Bloc A and Bloc G did not sign; Bloc B signed (Guardian, BBC 2025-02-11). No compute or capability limits in the text.

items.summary: Bloc A published a national AI action plan centred on 'winning the AI race' via deregulation, infrastructure and exports; it proposes no international limits on training compute or capabilities.
items.detail: 'Bloc A's AI Action Plan' (White House, 2025-07-23) and three accompanying executive orders. Not directly verified this run.

items.summary: Bloc B published a Global AI Governance Action Plan and proposed a world AI cooperation organisation; the plan emphasises capacity-building and multilateral norms, with no verification or compute-limit mechanism and no mention of military AI.
items.detail: Bloc B's Global AI Governance Action Plan released at WAIC Shanghai (2025-07-26); Premier Li Qiang proposed a World AI Cooperation Organization. RSIS notes it omits military applications.

items.summary: The UN General Assembly established, by consensus, a 40-member Independent International Scientific Panel on AI and an annual Global Dialogue on AI Governance; both are explicitly limited to the non-military domain and the panel's reports are 'non-prescriptive'. No limits or verification powers.
items.detail: UNGA resolution A/RES/79/325, adopted 2025-08-26 (verified via UN digital library).

items.summary: First in-person leaders' meeting since 2019 between the two blocs produced politically (not legally) binding trade de-escalation, including a mutual pause on export-control measures; AI risk, compute limits and military AI were not addressed.
items.detail: Trump-Xi meeting at Gimhae Air Base, Busan, 2025-10-30; White House fact sheet. Hudson Institute: security topics including arms control deferred.

items.summary: The only bilateral AI-security commitment remained the 2024 leaders' statement on keeping human control over nuclear-use decisions; analysts judged further steps unlikely in the near term. No negotiation on compute or capability limits was reported in 2025.
items.detail: RSIS IP25101 (2025) on AI/NC3; Brookings commentary. Status summary as of year-end, date nominal.
